name: Sheni-Ziriya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only known materials are wordlists/notes: Shimizu 1982 (Afrika und Ubersee wordlists) and Blench 2004 FEL note on the Seni/Ziriya; no grammar or phonology exists
earlier_scan.note: Moribund Jos Plateau lect; wordlist-level documentation only, no prosodic description

sources.citation: Blench, Roger (& Mallam Dendo). 2004. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Cambridge ms., 12 pp.
sources.note: Phonology section (3.1) describes eBoze only (vowels, consonants, tones); Sheni appears in Table 5 (tiSeni nominal plurals), App. 1 classification, App. 2 'The end of Ziriya and Kere', App. 3 'arm, hand'. The word 'stress' does not occur in the document.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record shen1251 (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less: Shimizu 1982; Williamson & Shimizu 1968 / Williamson 1973 BCCW).
sources.note: n/a; confirms no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for the language.

sources.citation: the Internet Archive CDX index of rogerblench.info (whole domain, filtered for Sheni/Seni/Ziriya) and of the East Kainji directory.
sources.note: Establishes that 'Notes on the ' (2008 and 2015 captures) is the only Sheni document Blench ever posted; his ~200-item tiSeni wordlist and any phonology were never put online.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages (submission draft; academia.edu 44092692).
sources.note: Phonology exemplified by Boze only ('All East Kainji languages so far studied have a relatively simple phonology'); tiSeni only for reduplicated plurals (Table 9). No mention of stress anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th edition. Entry 418 Sheni-Ziriya-Kere cluster.
sources.note: Bibliographic entry only: Source(s) Meek (ined.), Blench (2003); Refs Campbell & Hoskison (1969), Shimizu (1982). No phonology/grammar references exist for the cluster.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-033: retire [zir] Ziriya as equivalent to [scv] Sheni (adopted 2020-01-23).
sources.note: Nothing; administrative. Cites Blench & Nengel 2004, Shimizu 1982, Sommer 1992 as the whole evidence base.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press (NCAL 1).
sources.note: Sheni only in the family tree, Table 31 'Unpublished sources for Kainji languages' (Sheni: Blench) and a photo caption of the last Ziriya rememberer; nothing on Sheni prosody.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria (circulation draft, May 2012).
sources.note: Sheni only in the East Kainji classification, App. 1 (end of Ziriya) and the unpublished-sources table ('Sheni: Blench'); no Sheni phonology; 'stress' absent from the document.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & John Garah Nengel. 2004. Notes on the Seni people and language with an addendum on the Ziriya. Ms., Mallam Dendo Ltd / Jos University, 16 January 2004. 3 pp. (formerly rogerblench.info, East Kainji/Sheni)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Only prosodic remark (p. 2): 'Shimizu suggests that the tone system of Seni is High, Low, Downstep.. I began by recording tones but found they were rather unstable between speakers.' Rest is speaker census and reduplicative plural morphology; the ~200-word list itself is not included.
No phonology section; references are Ethnologue, Blench Atlas 2019, Temple 1922, Shimizu 1982, Blench 2004 notes, Blench 2012 Kainji overview.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2003 (unpublished). tiSeni wordlist, ca. 200 items, group elicitation at Gurjiya, 30 December 2003 (listed as 'Sheni: Blench' in Blench & McGill 2012 and Blench 2018 Table 31 of unpublished Kainji sources).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The most recent first-hand data (with Blench's tone transcriptions); never posted on rogerblench.info per the Internet Archive's index; would show whether any accentual pattern was noted.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1982. Ten more wordlists with analyses from the Northern Jos group of Plateau languages. Afrika und Übersee 65(1): 97-134 (Sheeni pp. 104 ff., Ziriya pp. 108 ff.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only published primary linguistic record of Sheni and Ziriya: tone-marked wordlists with phonological and noun-class 'analyses'; it is the source of the H/L/downstep tone claim and the only place a remark on stress vs tone could exist.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1979. Five wordlists with analyses from the Northern Jos group of Plateau languages. Afrika und Übersee 62: 253-271 (companion paper setting out the analytic template used in the 1982 article).

sources.note: Shows what Shimizu's 'analyses' cover (segment inventory, tone, noun classes) and whether he ever comments on stress for Northern Jos languages; helps interpret the 1982 Sheni analysis.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. (n.d., 1920s). Sheni wordlist, in 'Linguistic Notes', Vol. 2, Pt II: 509-516. Unpublished manuscript (Bodleian Library, Oxford).
